questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 ?
questions.explain: Count the 10s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 10, which is 5 × 10 = 50. Counting one group too many gives 6 × 10, which is 10 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 10 × 10 or 6 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Aisyah works out 1072 + 6274 in columns. One column makes 14, so she writes 4 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Aisyah works out 1072 + 6274 in columns. One column makes 14, so she writes 4 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 14 is the tens column: 7 + 7 = 14, and no other column reaches ten. 14 tens is 1 hundred and 4 tens, so the 4 stays in the tens column - worth 40 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The small 1 is worth 100. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: Aisyah works out 61 + 66 in her head. She makes 70 first. 61 + 66 = 70 + ?
questions.explain: To get from 61 up to 70 you need 9, so 9 is moved across from the 66. That leaves 66 − 9 = 57, and 70 + 57 = 127. Whatever you give to one number you must take off the other, or the total changes. You could have rounded the 66 up to 70 instead and taken that amount off the 61: it is the same total either way, so it lands on the same answer.

questions.explain: An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, so the ones card must be 0, 2 or 4. questions.explain: Write down the digits you are told: the thousands digit is 2 and the hundreds digit is 7. questions.stemText: Rectangle A is 12 cm by 7 cm. Rectangle B is 7 cm by 4 cm. How much longer is the perimeter of A than the perimeter of B?

Multiplying the cents and forgetting to carry them into the dollars gives $14.65.

questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 15 cm long and 9 cm wide. A notch 5 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 6 cm of edge before the notch and 4 cm after it, and the banner is still 7 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 6 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 4 + 9 + 15 + 9 = 52 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 5 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 5 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (15 + 9) + 2 × 2 = 52 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
